<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Tune the GLM-5.3-Flash recurrent KDA launch on SM90 using a wider value tile and fewer pipeline stages for small grids. This refresh preserves the launch-grid fix merged in #56974.

## Claims

- On SM90, use `BV = min(next_power_of_2(V), 16)` and `num_stages = 2` when `N * HV <= 32`; larger grids keep `num_stages = 3`. `num_warps` stays 1. Other architectures retain the existing configuration.
- The original H20 measurements showed 6.0–18.7% improvement per speculative-verification kernel call across TP4/TP8 and 1–64 requests. These are measurements from before this rebase, not fresh measurements on the updated branch.
- The regression test compares output and in-place state against the default launch configuration for decode and speculative shapes.

## Validation

### Current refresh — 2026-10-16

Rebased onto main `4f49b55c1f753183cec09f0a32f5e3a84467e1ec`. Current head: `a3aedea2107bfbc5e967792f9f8f41161f8a4838`.

- `git range-diff` reports the same patch as the previous head `38f0e370764a`; both changed source/test files are byte-identical Git blobs. The original SM90 tuning and bit-identity regression are unchanged.
- All upstream code is retained, including the `(N * HV, NV, NK)` launch-grid fix, large-grid regression, Triton pointer changes, ROCm/layout checks and prefill checkpoint tests.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, typos, CI test tethering and the current mypy hook (Python 3.11 target). An additional Python 3.12 mypy run passed for both changed files.
- Python syntax, LF line endings and `git diff --check` passed. This rebase required no manual conflict resolution.
- GPU tests, serving evaluation and performance measurements were intentionally not rerun; they are deferred until GPU capacity is available. The H20 results below remain historical and are not results for this head.

Local checks:

```powershell
$env:PYTHONUTF8 = '1'
uv run --offline --no-project --python D:/code/vllm/.venv/Scripts/python.exe python -m pre_commit run --files tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/kernels.py
uv run --offline --no-project --python D:/code/vllm/.venv/Scripts/python.exe python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12 tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/ops/third_party/kda/kernels.py
```

Pending GPU regression on SM90:

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py -v
```
### Previously reported H20 results

Configuration: `K = V = 128`, BF16 activations, FP32 recurrent state; baseline `BV=8`, `num_warps=1`, `num_stages=3`.

Speculative verification (`mtp=3`), per-call improvement:

| Requests | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
|---------:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8 | 16.5% | 18.7% | 17.7% | 14.3% | 6.0% | 6.4% | 9.2% |
| TP4 | 18.5% | 16.5% | 14.4% | 7.9% | 6.4% | 10.4% | 13.0% |

Pure decode at TP8: 10.1%, 10.2%, 8.1%, 4.1%, 1.6%, 1.3%, and 3.9% at the same request counts.

The original PR also reported:

- 9 recurrent KDA tests passed; output and state `max_abs_diff = 0.0` across the HV=8/HV=16 sweep.
- In-situ serving at 48 concurrent requests, 256 output tokens, speculative decoding enabled: kernel mean 50.4 → 48.7 µs across 2,312 calls, consistent across all eight TP ranks. The kernel accounted for approximately 4.3% of GPU kernel time.
- Greedy serving evaluation on 12 prompts × 256 tokens: no divergence beyond the serving stack's run-to-run nondeterminism; end-to-end throughput differences were within run-to-run variance. This PR claims a kernel improvement, without a demonstrated end-to-end throughput improvement.

## Details

The wider value tile amortizes repeated q/k/gate loads. The stage reduction is restricted to small grids; large grids retain the original stage count. The tuning was measured on H20; other SM90 devices were not benchmarked.

Duplicate-work check: the open-PR search for recurrent KDA found no other GLM-5.3-Flash SM90 launch-config PR. #56974 addresses the orthogonal gridDim.z limit and was merged on October 5. This refresh retains its `(N * HV, NV, NK)` launch grid and matching kernel indexing.

The earlier test-decorator resolution remains intact: the ROCm/CUDA layout check and the original NVIDIA-only SM90 test remain separate. Both changed files remain LF.

AI assistance was used for the original implementation and this rebase, static verification, and description update.

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** GPU validation on the refreshed branch has not been rerun; the original results and current local checks are distinguished above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps the reviewed implementation and preserves upstream behavior; local static checks pass.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes context, performance evidence, hardware limitations, and the AI-assistance disclosure.
</details>

Thanks for noting the relation to #56974 — agreed the two changes are orthogonal, and they compose: with this branch's two files normalised to LF, a three-way merge with #56974 applies without conflicts and both new tests in `test_kda_recurrent.py` survive.

One thing to fix before merge: both files in this PR are converted to CRLF line endings (`kernels.py` has 1399 `\r`, the test file 208). That is why the diff shows the whole files rewritten (+1399/−1377 and +208/−186) instead of the ~30 changed lines, and it will conflict textually with any other change to these files — including the launch-grid change in `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` and the added test in #56974 — whichever merges second. Re-saving the two files with LF endings should shrink the diff to the actual change.
Thanks ~. I've normalized both files to LF.

@@ -164,6 +167,32 @@ def test_fused_recurrent_kda_strided_inputs_bit_identical_to_contiguous(
     torch.testing.assert_close(state, state_ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    current_platform.is_rocm(),
+    reason="The SM90 launch dispatch only exists in the NVIDIA implementation",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("num_seqs", "query_len"), [(1, 1), (7, 1), (3, 3)], ids=["1x1", "7x1", "3x3"]
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_fused_recurrent_kda_sm90_launch_config_bit_identical(
+    monkeypatch, num_seqs: int, query_len: int
+):
+    """The SM90 dispatch (BV=16, small-grid num_stages=2) must be bit-identical
+    to the default configuration: num_warps stays 1, so the per-element
+    reduction order is unchanged."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    inputs, state = make_inputs(num_seqs, query_len, device)
+    state_ref = state.clone()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kernels, "_IS_SM90", False)
+    out_ref = run_kernel(inputs, state_ref)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kernels, "_IS_SM90", True)
+    out = run_kernel(inputs, state)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out, out_ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(state, state_ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
 @pytest.mark.skipif(

     reason="Both implementations require zero-copy token-strided layouts",

+    if _IS_SM90 is None:
+        _IS_SM90 = torch.cuda.is_available()
+        _IS_SM90 = _IS_SM90 and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (9, 0)
+    return _IS_SM90

+    # Shape-aware launch configuration, tuned on H20 (SM90) with K=V=128:
